newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bank licensing seen hit by political turmoil.
newsitem.headline: Thai bank licensing seen hit by political turmoil.

text.p: The decision by Thailand's finance minister to put on hold major policy decisions until he is replaced could further delay awarding of three new commercial banking licenses, analysts said on Monday.

Three groups headed by General Finance and Securities, MBK Properties and Development and Italian-Thai Development have already had applications endorsed by the cabinet, the first such awards in decades.
Final approval was now awaited from the Finance Ministry. A decision on the licences was due on earlier this year, but had been delayed since then.
Those who failed to make the shortlist included consortia headed by SITCA Investment and Securities, First City Investment, and The War Veterans' Organisation of Thailand (WVO).

Unelected Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda told reporters on Monday that he expected to be replaced after his patron Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa left office and so he would refrain from making key policy decisions.

Banharn was forced on Saturday to declare his resignation by key allies in his six-party coalition in return for their support at a no-confidence vote against him. Banharn won the vote after saying he would quit within seven days.

Bodi's decision could also affect the upgrading of foreign bank representative's offices into full offshore banking units, controls on foreign capital inflows and measures to shore up the ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce
Brett Williams, vice-president at Krungthai Thanakit, said further delays in the awarding of the bank licences would not improve the country's image in the eyes of world investors.

A public inquiry into the bank licence awards was set up last month following claims by Justice Minister Chalerm Yoobamrung that the award process was rigged. The minister later withdrew his allegations.
Analysts said that with Defence Minister Chavalit Yonchaiyudh widely tipped to succeed Banharn the already delayed new licensing process could come under further review.
Chavalit is leader of the New Aspiration Party, the second biggest party in the government coalition.
He is also WVO Chairman of the Veterans' Council and has supported the WVO's bid for a licence.

WVO Director General Euansak Chulachritta said the organisation had not received formal notification from the Finance Ministry that its bid had been rejected, and it would now wait for the political situation to unravel.
The WVO's original application was not approved because it planned to raise the required 7.5 billion baht million) capital by using a loan from state-owned Krung Thai Bank Plc
